themes.label: Motivation for nonlinear regime-switching trend modeling
themes.need: Someone modeling a nonstationary macroeconomic time series needs to know why a nonlinear discrete-regime-switching specification might be preferred over standard linear ARIMA, unobserved-components, or cointegration approaches to trend.

themes.label: Relation to prior regime-switching and filtering methods
themes.need: Someone considering this Markov-switching filter needs to understand how it relates to and improves upon prior regime-switching and filtering approaches: Goldfeld-Quandt switching regression, Aoki/Tong/Sclove specifications, the Liptser-Shiryayev continuous-time filter, and Wecker/Neftci turning-point methods.

themes.label: Markov trend model specification vs standard ARIMA
themes.need: Someone wants to specify a series trend as the outcome of a discrete two-state first-order Markov process, understand its AR(1) representation and statistical properties, and see precisely how the resulting composite process differs from a standard ARIMA model with normally distributed innovations.

themes.label: Forecasting and present value for Markov trend in levels
themes.need: Someone wants to compute optimal forecasts and discounted present values for a series whose trend follows a Markov process in levels, and to quantify how the current unobserved state has a permanent effect on future levels despite a state-independent long-run growth rate.

themes.label: Forecasting and present value for Markov trend in logs
themes.need: Someone wants to compute optimal forecasts and discounted present values for a series whose trend follows a Markov process in logs, via a vector-recursion and eigenvalue-decomposition approach, and to quantify the permanent effect of the current state on future levels.

themes.label: Combining Markov trend with autoregressive noise
themes.need: Someone needs to specify the complete observation equation combining the unobserved Markov trend component with a stationary autoregressive noise process, as groundwork for maximum-likelihood estimation when only their sum is observed.

themes.label: Nonlinear filtering algorithm and ML estimation
themes.need: Someone wants to implement the recursive nonlinear filter that produces probabilistic inference about the unobserved regime state from observed data, obtain the sample likelihood for maximum-likelihood estimation, initialize the recursion, and understand generalizations (n states, higher-order dynamics) and how the approach differs from Sclove (1983).

themes.label: Smoothing: full-sample regime inference
themes.need: Someone wants a more accurate, retrospective inference about which regime the process was in at each past date, using either the built-in r-lag smoother or the separate full-sample smoothing algorithm.

themes.label: ML estimates on US real GNP data
themes.need: Someone wants the maximum-likelihood parameter estimates obtained from fitting this model to postwar US real GNP data, their interpretation as business-cycle expansion/recession states, and how closely the four-lag smoother approximates the full-sample smoother.

themes.label: Dating historical business cycles from regime probabilities
themes.need: Someone wants to use the estimated smoothed regime probabilities as an objective algorithm for dating business-cycle peaks and troughs, compare the resulting dates to conventional NBER dating, and check implied expected recession/expansion durations against historical averages.

themes.label: Markov model encompasses linear ARIMA diagnostics
themes.need: Someone wants to understand why standard Box-Jenkins/AR(4) autocorrelation diagnostics on GNP growth look consistent with a simple linear process even though the true data-generating process is this nonlinear Markov model, i.e. whether the model satisfies the Hendry-Richard encompassing criterion, backed by theoretical autocovariance derivation and Monte Carlo evidence.

themes.label: Testable mean/variance predictions vs linear ARIMA
themes.need: Someone wants explicit statistical tests that do distinguish this Markov regime-switching model from a linear ARIMA/UC specification for GNP growth, specifically whether the lagged filtered regime probability significantly predicts the conditional mean and variance beyond a standard AR(4) model, with empirical test results.

themes.label: Business-cycle persistence: permanent effect on GNP level
themes.need: Someone wants to quantify the permanent effect of a business-cycle recession on the long-run level of real GNP implied by this Markov model, and compare it against prior linear-model estimates (Wold/ARIMA, unobserved-components, bivariate, nonparametric) collected from the literature, including a Jensen's-inequality correction for log-vs-level forecasts.

themes.label: Permanent-income-hypothesis implications
themes.need: Someone evaluating consumption or permanent-income theories wants the implied linear Wold-representation coefficient psi(1) for this Markov process, computed via its spectral density at frequency zero, and the effect of a certain recession on the discounted present value of future income.

unassigned.reason: Multi-claim preview paragraph stating (not questioning) that regime states map to the business cycle, match NBER dating, complement Nelson-Plosser/Campbell-Mankiw permanent-effect findings, and reinforce Neftci/Sichel asymmetry evidence. Verified: each claim is fully covered by a different downstream theme (t09 state interpretation, t10 NBER dating comparison, t13 permanent-effect/Table III comparison, t12 mean/variance asymmetry tests) with no single unresolved question posed for one resolving section — recap-shaped across four themes, not the intro-poses/section-resolves distributed pattern, so it stays unassigned rather than joining any one theme.
